entities.name: Presentation of the owner's previous score before rescoring
Anchoring bias from a visible previous score

relationships.evidenceLevel: Moderate — Group A (previous score shown first) 96% agreement, kappa 0.81, versus Group C (standard, no previous score) 79%, kappa 0.37; n=192 prospective
Moderate — the only validated tool for canine pruritus at the time of this study; measures owner-perceived severity, not disease
Moderate — separately validated (Strzok 2022), but NOT interchangeable with pVAS despite good correlation
Low — inherent to the design; the study measures internal agreement and cannot separate better assessment from a more self-consistent narrative
Low — retrospective analysis averaged 50.8% agreement (kappa 0.25), best at 30–60 day visit intervals (63%, kappa 0.355)

aiAgentFacts.fact: Owners shown their previous Pruritus Visual Analog Scale score before rescoring reached 96% agreement (kappa 0.81) with their own perception of improvement, versus 79% (kappa 0.37) for the standard method with no previous score shown.

The study measured agreement between score change and the owner's perception of improvement — NOT accuracy against the dog's actual pruritus. Anchoring to the visible previous score cannot be excluded as the mechanism.
In the retrospective arm across at least three consecutive real-world visits, average agreement was only 50.8% (kappa 0.25).
Agreement was highest at visit intervals of 30–60 days (63%, kappa 0.355), suggesting longer gaps degrade the comparison.
In the group completing both, pVAS and a 0–10 verbal scale did not differ significantly (P = 0.56).

A separate 2022 validation found the 0–10 verbal numeric scale valid for canine pruritus but NOT interchangeable with the pVAS (95% limits of agreement -2.0 to 2.57, outside the ±2 acceptability limit); 69% of clients preferred the pVAS.
This study enrolled dogs already under care for pruritus; it evaluates scale behaviour at follow-up and says nothing about detecting skin disease or about home scoring.

historyQuestions: Supported by the study's own manipulation: presenting the owner's previous score before asking for a new one substantially raises agreement with their perception of change — but see the anchoring caveat before treating this as improved accuracy.
redFlags: Not addressed — this study evaluates a severity scale's administration and identifies no red-flag findings.
differentialDiagnosesMentioned: Not addressed — dogs were already under care for pruritus; the study does not evaluate the cause of itch.
recommendedDiagnosticWorkups: Not addressed — no diagnostic workup is evaluated. The pVAS measures owner-perceived severity and is not a diagnostic instrument.

limitations: Outcome is agreement between score change and owner-perceived improvement — accuracy against the dog's true pruritus was never measured
Anchoring is an unexcluded alternative explanation for the Group A result and cuts directly against reading it as better observation
Single-centre study of dogs already under care for pruritus, using one scale
Real-world retrospective agreement was only 50.8%, far below the prospective figures, tempering how much the intervention effect transfers to ordinary practice
No home-scoring arm: the study describes clinic administration across follow-up visits, so it does not validate owner scoring at home
Group sizes for the five randomised arms are not reported in the abstract, so per-group precision is unknown
